sections.label: Merger effective date
sections.summary: The merger is intended to take effect on 1 April 2023 upon the passing of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Upon the passing of the Bill, we intend for the merger to take effect on 1 April 2023.

sections.label: ACRA Act amendment
sections.summary: Part 1 of the Bill amends the ACRA Act to let ACRA take on functions and powers currently with SAC.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Part 1 of the Bill amends the ACRA Act to allow ACRA to take on the functions and powers that currently reside with SAC.

sections.label: Accounting standards function for ACRA
sections.summary: The Bill gives ACRA the accounting standards setting function for companies, charities, societies and co-operative societies in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Bill confers the accounting standards setting function for companies, charities, societies and co-operative societies in Singapore on ACRA.

sections.label: Accountancy sector evolution and merger
sections.summary: The accountancy sector has evolved and will continue to, and the merger will better serve it and enhance Singapore's regulatory environment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Over the past decade, the accountancy sector has evolved from bookkeeping and auditing to include a myriad of other roles, such as corporate governance, insolvency and business advisory services.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: With emerging trends, such as sustainability, the accountancy sector will continue to evolve further.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We are committed to supporting the industry on this transformation journey and the merger will better serve the accountancy sector.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This will, in turn, enhance Singapore’s pro-business and trusted regulatory environment.

sections.label: Accountancy student intake and jobs
sections.summary: MOE data shows accountancy student intake fell from 1,508 in 2017 to 1,368 in 2020, while 6,000 to 7,000 jobs are expected by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: According to data published by MOE, the total intake of accountancy students at the Autonomous Universities has fallen from 1,508 in 2017 to 1,368 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Singapore's accountancy sector is expected to add 6,000 to 7,000 jobs by 2025, from a workforce of about 100,000 now.

sections.label: Chartered Accountants regulation
sections.summary: Regulation should require preparers of financial statements, especially in public interest entities, to be Chartered Accountants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To do this, there should be regulation whereby preparers of financial statements, especially those working in public interest entities, must be Chartered Accountants.

sections.label: Chartered Accountant signing requirement
sections.summary: Proposes compulsory signing of listed companies' financial statements by a Chartered Accountant and Chartered Accountant audit committee chairs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This will undermine public confidence and trust in both our accountancy profession, the regulatory system and Singapore’s credibility as a global financial centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I propose, for a start, to make it compulsory for financial statements of public-listed companies to be signed by the preparer who must be a Chartered Accountant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I would also suggest making it mandatory for the Audit Committee chairperson of a public-listed company to be a Chartered Accountant.

sections.label: Green finance skillsets needed
sections.summary: Corporate finance needs green finance and sustainability risk management skillsets, timely after the Carbon Pricing Bill passed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Those in corporate finance will need the skillsets in green finance and sustainability risk management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is timely, as this House has just passed the Carbon Pricing Bill yesterday.

sections.label: Accountancy Sector Roadmap launch
sections.summary: Accountancy is a key sub-sector of the Professional Services Industry Transformation Map and the Accountancy Sector Roadmap was launched.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Accountancy is a key sub-sector of the Professional Services Industry Transformation Map that was launched in January 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: In June 2018, the Accountancy Sector Roadmap was launched, charting an ambitious plan for the accountancy sector over the next five to 10 years to develop Singapore into a global accountancy hub.

sections.label: Accounting labour shortage reported
sections.summary: The Straits Times reported an acute labour shortage, with the Big Four raising salaries to retain talent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: In June this year, The Straits Times reported that the sector was experiencing an acute labour shortage, with the Big Four accounting companies raising salaries to retain talent.

sections.label: ACRA review under section 35G
sections.summary: ACRA may review DE's actions against the CA under section 35G upon being informed of DE's investigation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Generally, ACRA has the right to conduct a review of the actions taken by DE against the CA, under section 35G of the Act, upon being informed by DE of its investigation undertaken.

sections.label: Studying Chartered Accountant sign-off proposal
sections.summary: The proposal to require listed companies' financial statements signed by a Chartered Accountant needs further study on business costs and talent pool.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: On the suggestion to require all financial statements of listed companies to be signed off by a preparer who is a CA, we will have to study the proposal further as it would require careful consideration on areas, such as impact on business costs and the talent pool.

sections.label: Accountancy Workforce Review Committee
sections.summary: MOF and SAC convened the Accountancy Workforce Review Committee to recommend strategies to attract, develop and retain talent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: MOF and SAC have convened an Accountancy Workforce Review Committee, or AWRC, to recommend strategies to better attract, develop and retain talent.

sections.label: SCAQ programme review
sections.summary: Work is underway to review the SCAQ programme so the qualification and syllabus stay future-ready and industry-relevant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In this regard, work is currently underway to review the SCAQ programme to ensure that the qualification and syllabus stay future-ready and industry-relevant.

sections.label: SAC funding for ISCA certifications
sections.summary: SAC will provide funding support to ISCA to develop sustainability reporting and assurance certifications targeted for launch in the next two years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: On this front, SAC will be providing funding support to ISCA to develop sustainability reporting and assurance certifications targeted to be launched in the next two years.

sections.label: Committee recommendations public consultation
sections.summary: The Committee's work is well under way and recommendations will likely be issued for public consultation sometime next year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Committee's work is well under way and recommendations will likely be issued for public consultation sometime next year.
